The Mammography Quality Standards Act (MQSA) was implemented in 1995 to improve the quality of mammography services. Research has shown that, in the first year following MQSA implementation, there was a significant improvement in the quality of mammography care in North Carolina.

While specific studies are not mentioned, it is known that MQSA compliance among facilities led to improved patient outcomes and higher-quality care. This improvement may have resulted from increased adherence to federal regulations, such as those related to image acquisition, processing, and reporting.

Studies suggest that the benefits of MQSA go beyond just technical quality improvements. The act has also had a positive impact on patient satisfaction, with many patients reporting better experience and results following implementation.

However, it is essential to note that individual experiences may vary based on factors such as the specific population served, clinical protocols, and healthcare system characteristics. Further research can provide more insights into the long-term effects of MQSA on mammography quality in North Carolina.

In summary, based on available information, the MQSA has led to significant improvements in mammography quality in North Carolina, with patients experiencing better care, patient satisfaction, and potentially improved health outcomes.
